changes: Govinda: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other' — he was Śaṅkara's teacher and has no part in this copy; as_written cut down to the name compound

Viṭṭhala: residence read as 'vāstavya vasiṣṭhātīra āṣṭīgrāma' (living in Āṣṭīgrāma on the bank of the Vasiṣṭhā); 'śaṃtavarāḍa' treated as a probable family name, not a residence; scribe role kept but confidence lowered to medium, because 'yena pustakaṃ … kartavyaḥ' could also mean he had the copy made
Date: notes that 'saṃmata' stands for saṃvat and that the catalogue's VS 1982? does not match the colophon's 1872

persons.name: Viṭṭhala
persons.residence: Āṣṭīgrāma on the bank of the Vasiṣṭhā (vasiṣṭhātira āṣṭīgrāma)

purpose: for his own study of ātmavicāra (ātmavicārārtha)
notes: 'saṃmata' is a corruption of saṃvat; I take the year as VS 1872 (c. 1815/16 CE). The catalogue's 'VS1982?' does not match the colophon as quoted. The passage about Viṭṭhala is corrupt: 'vāstavyavasiṣṭhātira āṣṭīgrāma' probably means 'living in Āṣṭīgrāma on the bank (tīra) of the Vasiṣṭhā'. 'śaṃtavarāḍavena' probably contains a family name (Marathi Śaṃtavarāḍa/-e?) plus an instrumental ending. 'yena pustakaṃ … kartavyaḥ' does not say clearly whether Viṭṭhala wrote the copy himself or had it made. The scribe role follows the catalogue and the svārtha-type purpose.
